### Subject: Opinion on taxability of share premium received from a resident investor under Section 56(2)(viib)

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Zenith Innovations Private Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. We have not independently verified the facts provided to us. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Zenith Innovations Private Limited for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

Zenith Innovations Private Limited, which is not DPIIT-recognised as an eligible start-up, issued 10,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares to a resident angel investor at INR 1,200 per share against a fair market value of INR 950 per share as per a discounted cash flow valuation obtained by the Company.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the premium received in excess of fair market value is taxable in Zenith's hands as income from other sources under Section 56(2)(viib).

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 56(2)(viib)
- Rule 11UA


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Agro Portfolio (P) Ltd v. ITO (2018)
- VBHC Value Homes (P) Ltd v. ITO

## 6. Analysis

Since Zenith is not a recognised eligible start-up, the exemption from Section 56(2)(viib) is unavailable. The issue price of INR 1,200 exceeds the Rule 11UA fair market value of INR 950 by INR 250 per share, resulting in an aggregate excess of INR 25 lakh that is prima facie taxable. Following Agro Portfolio, a DCF valuation is not automatically displaced merely because actual performance later diverges from projections, so long as the assumptions were reasonable and bona fide when made; the strength of the Company's contemporaneous projections will materially affect the sustainability of the valuation on audit.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The excess premium of INR 25 lakh is taxable in Zenith's hands as income from other sources under Section 56(2)(viib), unless the valuation is revisited, or start-up recognition is obtained, prior to allotment.

**Confidence level:** Moderate; fairly arguable if the valuation assumptions are robustly documented
